newsitem.title: UK: Colombia 97/98 coffee output seen higher - Cardenas.
newsitem.headline: Colombia 97/98 coffee output seen higher - Cardenas.

text.p: The head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers Federation (FNC) said on Tuesday he expected the coming October/September 1997/98 crop to be a normal crop of 12.2 million bags.

Speaking at a producer/consumer meeting in London, Jorge Cardenas told Reuters the FNC would decide next week when to open July/September export registrations. Colombia produced 10.2 million bags in 1996/97.
"We expect to have a new crop of 12.2 million bags for the next crop year. That's the expectation but it's too early to say if it's true or not," Cardenas said.
He added that the crop would be on time, meaning that there would be no serious delay. This year's coffee harvest should start in October or November, he said.
"We need that coffee...we need a normal crop to stay in the market."

On Monday Cardenas said the FNC would reopen May/June coffee registrations for shipment of a maximum 500,000 60-kg bags by private exporters to Europe and Japan. Industry sources have said the May/June registrations were shut down suddenly on April 14.
